title: Split
subtitle: Ancient City by the Sea
summary: Split welcomed us from across its brilliant blue harbor, then drew us into a city where Roman columns, medieval stonework, family homes, cafés, and narrow passages all shared the same ancient walls. Diocletian's Palace was not a monument separated from daily life—it was the living heart of it.
heroImageAlt: Split's waterfront, historic center, and mountains viewed across the blue harbor
homepageSummary: Cross the harbor and step inside a Roman palace that has evolved into the lively, lived-in heart of modern Split.

sections.heading: A City Between Mountains and Sea
paragraphs: Split first appeared across a sweep of intensely blue water, its waterfront gathered beneath a long ridge of pale mountains. From the harbor, the city's layers were already visible: working docks in the foreground, the palm-lined Riva along the shore, and the bell tower rising above terracotta roofs.

Once ashore, we paused beside the promenade before entering the old city. The relaxed cafés and bright Adriatic light made the Riva feel like Split's front porch—a place where travelers arrived and local life unfolded at an unhurried pace.
sections.imageAlt: Steve and Dianne together at a waterfront café beside Split's palm-lined Riva
sections.imageCaption: Beginning our day beside the Riva

sections.heading: Inside a Living Roman Palace
paragraphs: Diocletian's Palace did not feel like a ruin with a city built around it. The palace had become the city. Roman columns framed a crowded Peristyle, ancient walls supported later buildings, and every passage seemed to connect one century with another.

The most remarkable details were often the ordinary ones: shuttered windows set into massive stone blocks, balconies above Roman masonry, and homes still occupying spaces shaped nearly two thousand years ago. History here was not preserved behind glass; it continued to be used.
sections.imageAlt: The columned Peristyle of Diocletian's Palace filled with visitors beneath a blue sky
sections.imageCaption: Roman architecture at the center of modern Split

sections.heading: The Cathedral Above the Palace
paragraphs: The Cathedral of Saint Domnius carried another of Split's extraordinary transformations. What began as Emperor Diocletian's mausoleum eventually became a Christian cathedral, while its tall bell tower grew into the defining landmark of the old city.

Seen above the layered palace walls, the tower made the city's long history feel almost tangible. Roman foundations, medieval additions, and present-day life occupied the same view, each era adapting what the previous one had left behind.
sections.imageAlt: Dianne looking toward the Cathedral of Saint Domnius bell tower above ancient palace walls
sections.imageCaption: Layers of Split beneath the cathedral bell tower

sections.heading: Following the Narrow Streets
paragraphs: Beyond the grand palace spaces, Split became intimate. We followed polished lanes into quiet courtyards, passed green shutters and sun-warmed stone, and looked up through narrow passages where plants and laundry softened the ancient walls.

Those smaller streets revealed the character we remembered most clearly. The palace was monumental, but it was also colorful, imperfect, and deeply human—a place where wandering without a route felt like the best way to understand it.
sections.imageAlt: A narrow residential alley in Split with warm walls, stone steps, and a red gate
sections.imageCaption: Everyday life tucked inside the old city's walls

reflections.author: Dianne
reflections.title: From Dianne's Journal
reflections.text: Walking through the palace changed the way I imagined an ancient site. It was full of movement and ordinary life, with homes and cafés woven directly into walls that had already stood for centuries.

reflections.author: Steve
reflections.title: Steve's Notes
reflections.text: Split rewarded every turn. The grand Roman spaces were unforgettable, but the quiet courtyards and lived-in passages made the city feel real rather than frozen in history.

quote.text: Split reminded us that history doesn't have to be behind museum glass. Here, people still live inside it every day.

highlights.title: Diocletian's Palace
highlights.description: One of the world's most remarkable Roman structures still serving as the heart of a modern city.

highlights.title: Riva Promenade
highlights.description: Split's waterfront is lined with cafés, palm trees, and beautiful Adriatic views.

highlights.title: Cathedral of Saint Domnius
highlights.description: Originally built as Emperor Diocletian's mausoleum, it later became one of the world's oldest cathedrals.

highlights.title: Old Town
highlights.description: Stone alleys, hidden courtyards, and centuries of history make every walk feel like an exploration.

tips.title: Explore on foot
tips.description: The historic center is compact and rewards slow exploration.

tips.title: Spend time on the waterfront
tips.description: The Riva offers a relaxing place to enjoy the city's atmosphere.

tips.title: Look upward
tips.description: Many of Split's architectural details are easy to miss unless you slow down and look around.

tips.title: Allow time to wander
tips.description: Some of the city's most memorable discoveries happen away from the busiest streets.
